subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module for a static 6-wheeled truck model, keeping it efficient without joints since the geometry can stay fixed in model space, roughly 11m long and 3m wide.

I'm sketching helper functions for boxes and cylinders to build the chassis, cab, outriggers, and wheel axles, working out proportions like wheel radius, axle spacing along three positions, and where the railgun turntable and barrel should sit on the rear deck pointing forward over the cab.

Adding the deck with side storage boxes, then building the turntable, turret base, and angled barrel with glowing coils and capacitor details, checking that the elevated barrel clears the cab.

Working out the geometry helpers for building the barrel from rotated cylinders and quaternion placement, I'll also pull in the glow kit for coils and lights, then lay out the twin rails and breech block positions along the local z-axis.

Still writing coil housing layout...

Now I'm adding capacitor bank cylinders on the turret sides with glow bands, trunnion cheeks with pivot cylinders, and elevation actuator rods connecting deck to breech. I'm also placing the turret base ring, rotating platform, and pivot coordinates, then starting on the four stabilizer outrigger legs.

Writing outrigger leg geometry...

Each wheel needs a tyre, hub, and bolts, bringing the total wheel part count to around 54. For the cab, I'm planning the windshield, roof sensor mast with radar dome, headlights, bumper with tow hook, grille, mirrors, antenna, and armor plating, plus deck details like side tool boxes and a rear power module box.

Setting up colors for olive drab, dark steel, tan, yellow, and glow accents in cyan and orange, then defining a helper function to generate box-shaped parts with position and color parameters.

Still writing geometry helpers...

Working out trunnion placement along x and the breech rotation offset, then laying out the turret platform: deck, turntable ring, and cheek dimensions, before positioning capacitor cylinders on the platform.

I'm now checking overall width constraints -- fitting capacitors flush against the outer cheeks while staying within the chassis envelope, then moving to hull width and wheel placement, making sure the fenders arch over the wheels without colliding with the deck edges.

Next I'm positioning the chassis beam and axle between the wheel hubs, adding a central differential sphere, then starting to block out the cab body dimensions sitting atop the frame.

Rethinking the cab shape to be cab-forward: a main body box spanning most of the length, a lower front wedge for the hood, and a separate engine hood section ahead of it, with a tilted windshield slab fitted into the sloped front.

Let me simplify instead: shorten the cab upper box and angle the windshield slab at roughly 34° from vertical, then define the cab side profile as an extruded shape for a cleaner silhouette.

Now I'm computing the windshield slab's position and orientation along the slope's outward normal, placing a thin tilted box aligned with that angled face.

I'm also placing side window boxes on both sides of the cab at the appropriate height and depth.

Then I'm adding the roof sensor mast with a radar dome and light bar, plus glowing headlight boxes and a dark grille panel at the front.

For the bumper I'm placing a wide box with dark coloring and yellow hazard stripes, along with armor skirt plates below. Behind the cab I'm positioning twin exhaust stacks as capped cylinders, and at the rear I'm laying out a deck platform with a generator box and vent slats.

Now I'm adding side tool lockers flanking the turret platform, tail lights at the rear, and simple markings including a white stripe and a circular emblem disc on the cab door made from layered cylinders.

I'm positioning the hazard-striped stabilizer beam with alternating yellow panels, sizing the beam and its outrigger legs with cylinders set along the chassis width.

Now I'm working out the hydraulic piston and octagonal foot pad geometry, plus the ball-joint connector, and adding a diagonal brace rod connecting the chassis to the leg at an angled offset for structural support.

I'll keep the gusset since it's cheap to add, then move on to other details: ground clearance underneath, towing points front and rear, a hatch and antenna on the platform top, and an orange beacon glow on the cab roof. I'm double-checking overall dimensions—height around 5.7m with the barrel, length roughly 10.2m plus barrel overhang—before detailing the barrel's ring housings, which decrease in size along its length with rails and centered housings.

Still working through the housing geometry...

Now I'm placing the muzzle box with its glow ring, computing the barrel tip position at pivot rotation for alignment checks, and adding counter-recoil buffer cylinders beside the breech along with elevation rod geometry mapped through a world-coordinate transform function.

I'm setting up helper functions for parts, boxes, and cylinders with axis-aligned orientation, then starting a wheel-building function.

Checking wheel placement at x=±1.55, making sure the axle height keeps the tire bottom flush with y=0 rather than sinking below ground, and confirming the pad geometry sits exactly on the surface. Now I'm planning the cab extrusion with its outline, thickness, color, and a slight bevel.

Adding roof details: a radar pole with a tilted dish near the front, and a light bar box positioned above with glowing orange ends — then writing it all out.
